title: Verdigris Bank — KYC automation pilot scratchbook
summary: Working notes from kickoff + two technical discovery calls with Verdigris Bank (Nov 10, Nov 14). Bank wants an automated KYC pipeline that meets strict data residency, audibility, and latency constraints. This doc collects high-level requirements, integration approaches, implementation risks, and immediate next steps.
body:
Context:
- Verdigris Bank (regional bank, heavy retail+SMB footprint) pursuing a 3-month KYC automation pilot for new account onboarding (web + branch capture).
- Primary goal: reduce manual review volume for routine cases (target 40% reduction) while maintaining auditability and regulatory traceability.
- Pilot scope: identity documents (passport, driver's license), proof of address (utility bill). OCR will be done upstream by partner (ABBYY / internal), Redwood will operate on extracted text + tokenized layout metadata.

Constraints and non-starters from customer: 
- No plaintext customer PII may be stored in non-customer-controlled storage. Must use VPC/private deployment or Dedicated with strict tenant isolation.
- Keys must be customer-managed (KMS + HSM preferred) and audit logs forwarded to Verdigris SIEM.
- Regulatory review requires deterministic model versioning and per-request provenance (model id, quantization profile, routing history).
- Target performance: peak concurrent documents ~1200/hr (burst to 3000/hr), steady-state 300/hr. 95th percentile latency target for classification/redaction: <= 300ms. Throughput objective favors batching but they want sub-second typical latency for web flows.

Recommended pipeline (two-stage):
1) Extraction & normalisation (partner OCR) -> produce text blocks, field candidates, confidence scores, and bounding boxes.
2) Redwood inference stage A: PII classification + field extraction (fast small model, locally hosted) for high precision blocking and redaction.
3) Redwood inference stage B: Dispute/edge-case triage using a larger, higher-quality model for borderline/confidence-low items. Stage B outputs fine-grained reasons for human reviewer and suggested correction.

Model & infra recommendations: 
- Deploy Redwood Private inside Verdigris VPC (control plane in Redwood-managed region, runtime in customer subnet) OR Dedicated with customer-managed keys if VPC not feasible.
- Use a small quantized model (e.g., 6B int8-equivalent) for stage A to hit the 300ms SLO and enable heavy batching; stage B can be a 13B/30B quantized variant with fallback to hosted Redwood models if on-prem capacity is exhausted.
- Enable prefix/KV cache for repeated template-heavy documents (driver's license layouts are extremely repetitive) to reduce tokens and latency for stage A.
- Autoscale GPUs with pre-warming policy for known branch-opening hours to handle bursts.

Integration gotchas observed / notes from calls: 
- OCR partner returns inconsistent field names and messy whitespace. We should normalise field keys at the integration layer and pass a consistent schema to Redwood (field_type, text, bbox, page).
- Scanned multi-page PDFs: the pipeline must preserve page order and associate fields with page-level bounding boxes for provenance.
- Bank's legal team insists on per-request non-repudiable audit entries; need request id + model hash + routing decision captured in logs forwarded to SIEM.
- Branch tablet captures sometimes include photos rotated 90deg; OCR partner sometimes fails — must include explicit rotate-and-retry pre-step (local client).
- Edge-case: laminated IDs reflect light and OCR introduces spurious characters; stage A should be conservative (favor human review) and stage B should offer correction suggestions rather than auto-approve.

Evaluation & success metrics for pilot: 
- Reduction in manual-review volume (%) by category (ID vs address). Target: 35–45% overall first month.
- False negative rate on fraud/forgery indicators (critical). Target: <1% for high-risk flags.
- Mean time to decision for web flows (ms) and human queue size.
- Cost per processed document (Cloud cost + infra amortized).

Security / compliance checklist (customer must sign off):
- KMS/HSM integration test plan scheduled before ingest of any real PII.
- SIEM log format and endpoint for forwarding (LLP+syslog).
- Data retention policy: redacted text stored for 30 days, raw OCR output never leaves customer subnet unless explicitly allowed.

People notes / voices: 
- Verdigris: Priya (head of onboarding), Nate (platform infra), Alvaro (compliance). Priya pushes to minimize manual touches. Alvaro is conservative and will block any approach that stores raw images off-site.
- Customer success (Redwood): Ravi to lead pilot coordination. Solutions eng: Lena (owner) + Maya (infra lead).

Morning after call quick sketch of timeline (rough):
- Week 0: NDA + pilot SOW, legal alignment on KMS & data flow (1 week).
- Week 1–2: Infra prep (VPC subnet, HSM, SIEM endpoints), OCR integration contract, sample data transfer in controlled sandbox.
- Week 3: First integration run with synthetic/sample docs; tuning stage A thresholds.
- Week 4–6: Gradual live ramp with branch + web, monitor accuracy and human-review reduction.

Notes on pricing / commercial:
- Customer prefers committed Dedicated pool that they can attach to for predictability. They asked for a T-shirt estimate for 6-month pilot at ~ $40k–75k/mo depending on infra (private with HSM on their cloud vs Redwood-managed dedicated). Need to convert to actual quote after capacity planning and region selection.

Misc technical ideas to explore (brainstorm):
- Localized regex and deterministic parsers for MRZ/typical ID fields to reduce inference load.
- Hybrid approach: run deterministic checks first; only call ML models for low-confidence cases.
- Use evaluation prompts with anchored examples to force model to output JSON table for field-level provenance.

End of scratchbook body.
action_items: Lena: Draft pilot SOW template and share with Ravi by 2025-11-20
Ravi: Schedule legal sync with Verdigris (Alvaro) to confirm KMS/HSM acceptance; target 2025-11-19
Maya: Produce infra diagram for VPC-based Private deployment + SIEM forwarding by 2025-11-21
Jonah: Create synthetic dataset (500 varied ID/doc images) and upload to sandbox for initial runs by 2025-11-24
Ravi & Priya (customer): Decide on Dedicated vs Private option after week-1 infra tests (decision meeting 2025-11-25)
open_questions: Can Verdigris allow redacted OCR text to be stored outside the subnet for pilot analytics?
Which cloud region will the customer's VPC be in (affects latency and pricing)?
Do they have existing HSM with API we can integrate, or do we need to provision via Redwood's partners?
Exact peak TPS expectation for the branch batch upload window (they gave hour-level estimates; need minute-level distribution)
decisions: Pilot will aim for a two-stage inference pipeline (fast conservative model + higher-quality triage model)
Customer requires customer-managed keys and SIEM forwarding; plan private deployment options first
